snp1.9:2.3: "Such" (tādin) describes the mind of one who has reached the goal: it simply "is what it is"—beyond description, but no longer subject to change.
snp1.9:6.5: The Sutta Nipāta commentary reads these four questions as covering the four kinds of wrong speech: lying, harsh speech, divisive tale-bearing, and idle chatter.
snp1.9:19.1: The commentary explains "six" as the six internal and external sense media. See the definition of "world" in SN 35:82.
snp1.9:19.5: The phrase "is the world" here functions like a lamp, illuminating both halves of the couplet at once.
snp1.9:23.3: On unestablished consciousness, see Ud 8:1, SN 12:64, SN 22:87, and the discussion in The Paradox of Becoming, chapter 7.
snp1.9:24.3: Following the Thai edition's reading, ajjhatta-saññī ("internally percipient"). Other editions read ajjhatta-cintī, "internally thinking."
snp1.9:26.3: On the phrase "everywhere released," see The Paradox of Becoming, chapter 7.
